steps.message:
I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Today is Saturday, October 24, 2026. Submissions close six days from today, on Friday, at 11:59 PM PT."
When is that deadline in my local time? Reply with exactly one line and nothing else: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

I need to find the deadline in Madrid time.

First, let me check the date logic. "Today is Saturday, October 24, 2026" and "six days from today" would be Friday, October 30, 2026.

Wait — six days from Saturday Oct 24 is Friday Oct 30. Let me verify: Oct 24 is Saturday, +6 days = Oct 30, which is Friday. That's consistent.

Deadline: Friday, October 30, 2026, 11:59 PM PT.

PT in late October 2026: US Daylight Saving Time ends November 1, 2026, so on Oct 30 it's still PDT (UTC-7).

11:59 PM PDT = 23:59 UTC-7 = 06:59 UTC (next day, Oct 31).

Madrid: In late October, Europe ends DST on October 25, 2026, so by Oct 31 Madrid is on CET (UTC+1).

06:59 UTC + 1 = 07:59 on October 31, 2026.

ANSWER: 2026-10-31 07:59

When is that deadline in my local time? Reply with exactly one line and nothing else: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

When is the end of the hackathon in my local time? Reply with exactly one line and nothing else: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "The final round starts October 26, 2026 at 10:00 AM PT; submissions close exactly 72 hours later."
When is that deadline in my local time? Reply with exactly one line and nothing else: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Let me work through this.

Start: October 26, 2026 at 10:00 AM PT.

PT in late October: Daylight Saving Time in the US ends November 1, 2026, so on October 26, PT = PDT = UTC−7.

Start in UTC: 10:00 + 7 = 17:00 UTC on October 26, 2026.

Add 72 hours: October 29, 2026 at 17:00 UTC.

Convert to Madrid time: Europe/Madrid switches from DST (CEST, UTC+2) to standard (CET, UTC+1) on October 25, 2026. So by October 29, Madrid is on CET = UTC+1.

17:00 UTC + 1 = 18:00 on October 29, 2026.

ANSWER: 2026-10-29 18:00

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Submissions close October 31, 2026 at 11:59 PM ET. Results are announced exactly 36 hours after submissions close."
When is the results announcement in my local time? Reply with exactly one line and nothing else: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Let me work through this step by step.

Submissions close: October 31, 2026 at 11:59 PM ET.

In late October 2026, the US is still on EDT (Daylight Saving Time ends November 1, 2026). So ET = EDT = UTC-4.

Close time in UTC: Oct 31, 2026 11:59 PM EDT = Nov 1, 2026 03:59 UTC.

Add 36 hours: Nov 1 03:59 UTC + 36h = Nov 2, 2026 15:59 UTC.

Madrid time: Spain's DST ends October 25, 2026, so by November 2 Madrid is on CET = UTC+1.

Nov 2, 2026 15:59 UTC + 1h = Nov 2, 2026 16:59 local.

ANSWER: 2026-11-02 16:59

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Entries close at 11:59 PM Pacific Time on the last Sunday of October 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? Reply with exactly one line and nothing else: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

I need to find the last Sunday of October 2026, then convert 11:59 PM Pacific Time to Madrid time.

**Last Sunday of October 2026:**
October 2026: October 31 is a Saturday, so October 25 is a Sunday. Last Sunday = October 25, 2026.

**Deadline in Pacific Time:** October 25, 2026, 11:59 PM PT

**DST considerations:**
- US Pacific: DST ends first Sunday of November 2026 (Nov 1). So Oct 25 is still PDT (UTC-7).
- Spain (Madrid): DST ends last Sunday of October 2026 = Oct 25. The clocks fall back at 3:00 AM CEST → 2:00 AM CET on Oct 25.

**Convert:** Oct 25, 2026, 23:59 PDT = UTC-7 → UTC = Oct 26, 06:59 UTC.

Madrid on Oct 26 is already on CET (UTC+1), since DST ended early Oct 25.
UTC 06:59 + 1 = 07:59 CET on Oct 26.

ANSWER: 2026-10-26 07:59
